items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: Frank Wess wrote a number of things for the band... I was on the band four and a half years

ctx.x: I mean they had so many great ones.

Well Neal Hefti, Neal Hefti was absolutely wonderful. Frank Foster. Frank Wess wrote a number of things for the band, wonderful. Let me see, John Clayton wrote a few things for the Basie band that were great. So did Bobby Plater. And let me see some of the © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

other, Sammy Nestico is just one of my all time favorite Basie writers. He’s one of my all time favorite writers anyway, he’s a great, great arranger, just marvelous. Chico O’Farrill did a number of things for the band that were just great. Unfortunately we never played any of Oliver Nelsen’s arrangements when I was in the band. We played a couple of Thad Jones arrangements which were great, they were really wonderful. But there were a lot of the charts from earlier days that I really wanted to play with the band…

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I have to tell you I forgot about that really. But that is a very good album specifically because of the giants that are all on there... They play so beautifully

ctx.x: Milt Hinton, what a team, Urbie Green, Bucky Pizzarelli, Joe Temperley, Frank Wess, Joe Wilder, and Dick Hyman charts. And actually this one I would have on my desert island list.

That’s a good one. I have to tell you I forgot about that really. But that is a very good album specifically because of the giants that are all on there that I’m just trying to keep time for, and not get in their way. They play so beautifully, they play so musically, they play so, just magnificent.
